name: Scandinavian modern tableware
summary: Plain, stackable tableware from the factories of Finland and Sweden. Artists on the staff of the factory design simple forms in a few shapes, glaze them in satin or matt colours, and add a quiet hand mark.

philosophy.core_thesis: A few plain shapes that stack, a warm satin glaze and a quiet hand mark make tableware that is made in a factory but feels human.
design_principles: Design a service of a few shapes that are fit for every meal, and let them stack in a column.
Make each piece a plain solid, and leave the surface to the glaze.
Glaze in a satin or matt colour: white, sand, grey, olive or a deep blue.
Add a small relief of ribs or a thin incised line, and no more.
Let an artist, not a stylist, design the service, and put the name in the base.
Make the factory a studio: the artist works on the line and on one-off pieces.
Choose a wall 4 to 6 mm thick, which is strong enough for daily use and stacking.
anti_patterns: A gilt rim and a floral pattern
A glossy bright colour in the manner of the American diner
A heavy, rustic wall with a rough glaze
A sharp, cold geometric shape with no warmth

form.shape: Flat plates, stacking bowls, shallow serving dishes, covered tureens, and cups and jugs that stack.
form.profile: A plain solid with a soft edge; the bowl has a straight wall and a flat base, and the plate has a narrow rim.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat base with a small foot ring, glazed or bare; the rim is round and plain.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 17 to 26 cm and wall 4 to 6 mm thick; the pieces stack in one column.
rules: Make every piece fit the next in a stack.
Keep the edge round and plain, and the surface quiet.
Give each piece one single use, and name it by that use.

bodies.rule: Use a strong stoneware or earthenware that stacks and stands the daily wash. Wood is for trays and lids. Do not use a thin porcelain with gold: the style is warm and plain.

methods: incising and wax-resist decoration by hand
forming.joins: Handles are cast with the body or luted with slip; a wooden lid or tray is made to fit.
forming.details: A small hand mark: a brush stroke, an incised line, or a signature of the artist in the base.

glaze.pattern: Plain; a ring of fine ribs, a thin incised band, or a small leaf or a stroke in a second tone.
glaze.gloss: Satin to matt, about 20 to 55 GU.
glaze.wear: The glaze keeps a quiet sheen and shows a mark of the stack at the rim; the tone stays even.

palette.strategy: Warm, quiet colours in a satin glaze: white, sand, grey, olive and a deep blue, with a dark brown for the hand mark.

firing.kiln: A gas or electric tunnel kiln; a biscuit firing and a glaze firing in clean air.
firing.scale: A large factory with an art department, in which artists make the line and the one-off pieces.
firing.signs: The artist name in the base, a quiet sheen, and a light hand mark under the glaze.

pieces.form: Flat plate with a narrow plain rim, in a stacking series, in a satin white glaze
Stacking bowl with a straight wall and fine ribs, in an olive matt glaze
Small plate with a thin incised line at the rim, in a sand satin glaze
Oval dish with a plain wall, in a grey matt glaze

positive: thin incised line and fine ribs
artist's hand mark under the glaze

emotion.target_response: A warm, quiet ease: the viewer sees plain stacked pieces and a soft glaze, and thinks of a calm everyday table.

use_cases: a calm Nordic kitchen or table scene
a museum label on 1950s Finnish and Swedish ceramics
avoid_when: the brief wants gilt or painted ornament
the brief wants bright gloss colour
the brief wants a rustic hand-thrown look

modifiers.how: Change the body to white porcelain, drop the hand mark, and use a bright clear glaze.
Change to hand-thrown stoneware with a matt glaze, and allow an uneven rim.
Replace the plain solids with a soft free-form curve and a muted colour glaze.
